target_customer: Shipowners and operators that must cut CO2 on existing vessels under new global regulation
problem: Existing ships cannot easily switch fuels, so shipowners need a way to cut exhaust CO2 on current vessels to meet regulation.
business_model: Hardware sales or leasing of retrofit carbon capture containers plus handling of the captured carbonate at ports
product_category: Climate hardware: onboard carbon capture for ships

founders.name: Alisha Fredriksson
founders.background_notes: YC page: launched a climate program and built global partnerships at Generation.

founders.name: Roujia Wen
founders.role: Co-founder and CTO (later listed as co-founder and advisor)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (May 2022) says she worked on AI products at Amazon. Not listed on the YC page; named in TechCrunch and on the company site.

investors: UK Government Clean Maritime Demonstration Competition round 6
European Space Agency (EUR 1.5 million award per the company site headline)

competitors.name: K Line
competitors.what: Japanese shipping firm developing ship-based carbon capture with a solvent approach

competitors.name: Value Maritime
competitors.what: Dutch company with a Filtree scrubber plus CO2 capture module
competitors.traction_then: First vessel, Visser Shipping's Nordica, fitted in October 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: A calcium looping style capture container that survives sea conditions, integrates with ship exhaust and handles solid carbonate offloading is a hard chemical engineering and hardware problem for a small team; pilots on commercial ships were still ahead in 2022.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary process and ship trials take years, and shipowner relationships (Eastern Pacific Shipping is an investor) help, but large engine and marine suppliers can field capture systems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wartsila made its onboard carbon capture commercially available in May 2025 and others piloted systems, but Seabound completed commercial scale units in early 2026 and trials with Hapag-Lloyd and a cement carrier.

market_need_then: In May 2022 TechCrunch reported six letters of intent with major shipowners and the company cited new global regulations; shipping is a large CO2 emitter with a slow fleet turnover.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and urgent: short imperative headlines such as We Fit, We Capture and Don't wait for future solutions

branding.brand_signature: We Fit, We Capture, We Offload tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch (2022), Business Insider (2023) and The Guardian (2025) is linked from the YC page; no evidence of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated international press and a clear verb-driven message, but no source on brand recognition outside shipping. Another company called Seabound exists in tourism media.

outcome_analysis: Seabound raised a $4.4 million seed led by Lowercarbon in May 2022, ran sea trials on commercial ships, won UK and European grants, and completed its first full scale commercial units in February 2026 with a cement carrier customer. Regulation pushing shipping decarbonisation is the tailwind, while Wartsila and others entering in 2025 show the risk from larger suppliers. It is active and pre-scale on commercial revenue.
notes: Aggregators disagree on the seed: a VC Breakfast Club headline says 1.1 million dollars and another tracker says an 11 million grant round, while TechCrunch says 4.4 million; TechCrunch is used. Total funding estimates range from 6.8 to 13.06 million dollars across aggregators and are not used. The ESA award is stated as EUR 1.5 million in a headline on the company site, dated from a February 2026 news item, so the USD amount is null. The company site also mentions an earlier win in CMDC round 3 with no amount. A Series A label on one aggregator page is unverified. The Value Maritime Nordica fitting in October 2021 is from a later trade article summary. Names of other advisors omitted.
